data.text: This amendment is considered to be substantial based on the criteria set forth in Article 10(a) of Directive 2001/20/EC of the European Parliament and the Council of the European Union, the US Food and Drug Administration's (FDA) regulation at 21 CFR part 312.30(b), and any applicable local regulations.
data.sourceSection: Protocol Amendment Summary of Changes Table

data.text: The main reason for preparation of this amendment was to clarify study procedures occurring across different sites in the US, so as to facilitate participant recruitment across different regions of the US, and to lessen inconvenience for participants without compromising the quality of the study.
data.sourceSection: Protocol Amendment Summary of Changes Table - Overall Rationale for the Amendment

data.text: Number of days changed from 30 days to 21 days in the following sentence: the inhibitory effect of zinc on intestinal copper absorption is expected to be minimal 30→21 days after discontinuation of zinc. Rationale: To align the number of days with the mention of zinc discontinuation elsewhere in the protocol.
data.sourceSection: Protocol Amendment Summary of Changes Table - Section 4.2 Scientific Rationale for Study Design

data.text: Addition of text to the footnote to state that procedures specific to screening sites (only in the US) detailed in Section 8. Rationale: As per Section 8 (below).
data.sourceSection: Protocol Amendment Summary of Changes Table - Section 1.3 Schedule of Activities (SoA), Table 1

data.text: Addition of text applicable only to the US that details the possibility for sites in the US to only perform screening procedures and not any of the remaining study procedures. Rationale: To facilitate participant recruitment across different regions of the US and to lessen inconvenience for participants without compromising the quality of the study.
data.sourceSection: Protocol Amendment Summary of Changes Table - Section 8 Study Assessments and Procedures

data.text: Samples collected within ± 10% or 30 min, whichever is less, of the scheduled time will not be considered a protocol deviation.
data.sourceSection: Section 8.5 Pharmacokinetics

data.text: Excess/additional samples may be stored for up to 5 years and used for PD and/or diagnostic biomarker development and research to understand the pathways associated with the mechanism of action of ALXN1840. These samples will not be used for genetic analyses (ie, RNA or DNA analyses).
data.sourceSection: Section 8.5 Pharmacokinetics

data.text: A single biobanked serum sample will be collected predose from each participant to serve as a retained sample during the study. Samples will remain on site and will be discarded following the completion of the clinical study report. The sample will not be used for genetic testing.
data.sourceSection: Section 8.3.6 Retained and Biobanked Sample

data.text: Medical Monitor Name and Contact Information can be found in the Study Contact List.
data.sourceSection: Title Page

data.text: Participants may be discharged from the CRU on Day 9 and return on Day 22 or Day 23 (predose); all procedures will start on Day 23. To ensure flexibility, the Outpatient Period during Treatment Period 1 may be extended up to an additional 14 days with Investigator approval.
data.sourceSection: Section 4.2 Scientific Rationale for Study Design

data.text: During the Outpatient Period, participants will use SMS text messaging to confirm study intervention administration.
data.sourceSection: Section 4.2 Scientific Rationale for Study Design

data.text: At the CRU's discretion, participants may remain in the CRU during the outpatient period for safety or to maintain the integrity of the conduct of the study.
data.sourceSection: Section 4.2 Scientific Rationale for Study Design

data.text: A cannula may be placed to minimize needle sticks; however, a catheter may not be left in place for longer than 72 hours and should be flushed a minimum of every 8 hours.
data.sourceSection: Table 3: Potential Risks and Mitigation Strategy - Study Procedures

data.text: Rescreened participants are not required to reconsent as long as they have signed the latest version of the ICF.
data.sourceSection: Section 5.4 Screen Failures

data.text: Blood pressure and heart rate measurements should be preceded by at least 5 minutes of rest for the participant in a quiet setting without distractions (eg, television, cell phones). Ideally, the same arm for each participant should be used for measurements.
data.sourceSection: Section 8.2.2 Vital Signs

data.text: If vital signs are abnormal as defined by inclusion/exclusion criteria, 2 additional vital signs measurements will be made. The average of the 3 vital signs measurements will be recorded in the CRF and used to determine participant eligibility.
data.sourceSection: Section 8.2.2 Vital Signs

data.text: As this study is an exploratory study, no formal hypothesis testing is being conducted. Study results will be summarized using descriptive statistics.
data.sourceSection: Section 9.1.1 Primary Hypothesis

data.text: All SAEs will be recorded and reported to Alexion or the designee immediately and under no circumstance should this exceed 24 hours. The Investigator will submit any updated SAE data to Alexion within 24 hours of it being available.
data.sourceSection: Section 8.3.1 Time Period and Frequency for Collecting AE and SAE Information

data.text: Limited nonclinical data on copper elimination with tetrathiomolybdate suggested copper excretion may be at least maintained or increased with repeated dosing (refer to the current IB).
data.sourceSection: Section 4.2 Scientific Rationale for Study Design

data.text: Darwich, 2014 cited as reference for physiologic turnover of human gastrointestinal epithelial cells being 3-5 days, supporting the change from 30 to 21 days for zinc inhibitory effect.
data.sourceSection: Section 4.2 Scientific Rationale for Study Design / Amendment Summary

data.description: Original protocol for Phase 2 open-label study ALXN1840-WD-204 to assess copper and molybdenum balance in participants with Wilson Disease treated with ALXN1840
First amendment to protocol ALXN1840-WD-204
Second amendment to protocol ALXN1840-WD-204
Third amendment to protocol ALXN1840-WD-204

US-specific sub-amendment to Amendment 3 of protocol ALXN1840-WD-204. Primary changes include: clarification of study procedures for US screening sites added to SoA Table 1 footnote, correction of zinc inhibitory effect timeframe from 30 to 21 days in Section 4.2, and addition of US-specific screening site procedures in Section 8. Conducted to facilitate participant recruitment across different regions of the US and lessen participant inconvenience without compromising study quality. Considered substantial per Article 10(a) of Directive 2001/20/EC and FDA regulation at 21 CFR part 312.30(b).
